import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 594

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/594](https://www.erdosproblems.com/594)
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in
  Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968)
  (1969), 27-35.
- [EHS74] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A. and Shelah, S., On some general properties of chromatic
  numbers. Topics in topology (Proc. Colloq., Keszthely, 1972) (1974), 243-255.
-/

open Cardinal
open scoped Cardinal

namespace Erdos594

/--
**Erdős Problem 594** (Erdős–Hajnal [ErHa66], [Er69b]):

Does every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$ contain all sufficiently
large odd cycles?

The answer is **Yes**, proved by Erdős, Hajnal, and Shelah [EHS74].

A graph has chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$ (i.e. uncountable chromatic number)
if and only if it admits no proper colouring with countably many colours; this is
encoded as `IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ)`. The conclusion states that there is some
$N$ such that for every $k \geq N$ the graph contains a cycle of odd length $2k + 1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_594 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ) →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, N ≤ k →
        ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length = 2 * k + 1 := by
  sorry

/--
The earlier result of Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa66]: every graph with chromatic number
$\geq \aleph_2$ contains all sufficiently large odd cycles.

Chromatic number $\geq \aleph_2$ is encoded as the nonexistence of a proper colouring
with any set of at most $\aleph_1$ colours.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_594.variants.erdos_hajnal (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (h : ∀ (α : Type), #α ≤ ℵ_ 1 → IsEmpty (G.Coloring α)) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, N ≤ k →
      ∃ (v : V) (w : G.Walk v v), w.IsCycle ∧ w.length = 2 * k + 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check for the encoding of "chromatic number $\geq \aleph_1$": a countably
colourable graph, such as the empty graph on $\mathbb{N}$, does not satisfy the
hypothesis `IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ)`.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_594.variants.bot_countably_colorable :
    ¬ IsEmpty ((⊥ : SimpleGraph ℕ).Coloring ℕ) := by
  rw [not_isEmpty_iff]
  exact ⟨SimpleGraph.Coloring.mk (fun _ => 0) (by simp)⟩

end Erdos594

reformulations.difference: Expresses uncountable chromatic number as `IsEmpty (G.Coloring ℕ)` and expresses eventual odd-cycle containment using closed walks satisfying `IsCycle`, of lengths `2 * k + 1` for `N ≤ k`. EHS74 Theorem 3 uses χ(G) > ω and lengths 2j+1 for n < j.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any coloring with a countable palette can be recolored into ℕ, so absence of an ℕ-coloring is exactly chromatic cardinal at least ℵ₁. For lengths at least 3, Mathlib's `IsCycle` walks are equivalent to ordinary, not necessarily induced, copies of cycle graphs. Every sufficiently large odd length is 2k+1; the existential threshold absorbs both this reindexing and the strict/non-strict bound difference. These equivalences, including the universally quantified statement with `chromaticCardinal` and cycle-graph containment, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the strict-threshold equivalence was also proved in /workspace/review/threshold.lean.

reformulations.difference: Replaces the source's chromatic-number bound χ(G) ≥ ℵ₂ with nonexistence of proper colorings into every type of cardinality at most ℵ₁.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since ℵ₂ is the successor cardinal of ℵ₁, χ(G) ≥ ℵ₂ holds exactly when no palette of cardinality at most ℵ₁ admits a proper coloring. The quantification includes representatives of all such cardinals and is not vacuous. A graph always admits its vertex set as a palette, so the chromatic-cardinal definition has a nonempty defining set. The hypothesis equivalence and the full statement's equivalence to chromatic-cardinal bounds and eventual odd-cycle containment were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős and Hajnal, On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems (1966), definitions in §2 and Problem 7.6 with its following remark, p. 77: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1966-07.pdf
Erdős, Problems and results in chromatic graph theory (1969), particularly p. 31: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf

Erdős, Hajnal, and Shelah, On some general properties of chromatic numbers (1974), chromatic-number definition on pp. 244–245 and §4, Theorem 3, pp. 250–251: https://shelah.logic.at/files/203571/Sh-32.pdf
Shelah archive bibliography and publication metadata: https://shelah.logic.at/paper-list/ and https://shelah.logic.at/papers/32/
review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The positive answer and both `research solved` tags are supported by the cited primary literature. Independent Lean checks established satisfiability of both research hypotheses using complete graphs, excluded empty/countable vertex graphs from the main hypothesis, and tested genuine versus repeated cycle walks. The existing edgeless-graph sanity check and the scratch equivalence proofs have no `sorryAx` dependency. The live erdosproblems.com page returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers; its current presentation could not be inspected, so verification used all three cited primary papers instead.
